notes: Phase order mirrors the recipe's variant chain — variant 1 (clean /exit) → variant 2 (SIGKILL mid-idle) → variant 3 (SIGKILL mid-turn). Each variant's process_exited anchors the next variant's session birth (restart mints a fresh session id/cwd/PID). Muse's own session.end record is not what drives any of these transitions — the daemon's generic PID-liveness watch (kqueue on the bound PID) is, so the phases below are agent-agnostic in mechanism even though the transcript content that produces them is muse-specific. Anchors are scoped to the 3 TOP-LEVEL session ids; a reminder-agent subagent session (format-spec §9) may also appear and is out of scope for this spec. same_session_as pins added post-record (2026-09-14, recording 2026-09-14-05-51-48-ish): the ORIGINAL spec had none, and a live run proved the vacuous-pass risk this creates is not hypothetical — v2_exit's bare process_exited search (no session pin) matched session 3's proc-<pid> shadow row's exit instead of session 2's own, purely because it was the chronologically next process_exited event in the curated stream. KNOWN RACE (not marked known_failing on THIS committed recording -- see why below): once pinned  to their own session, both SIGKILL variants' process_exited is racy against processlifecycle's PID-keyed `watched map[int]string` (core/adapters/inbound/agents/processlifecycle/monitor_darwin.go, `m.watched[pid] = sessionID`, last-write-wins) — every restarted muse session ALSO spawns a generic proc-<pid> presession watching the SAME OS pid (wiring.go's unconditional per-adapter scanner), and whichever of the two registrations (the real session's, or its own presession shadow's) re-registers the kqueue watch LAST wins the map slot, so the kqueue NOTE_EXIT callback can fire for the WRONG session id. Directly confirmed live, twice, in two independent recordings: attempt 1 (discarded, pre-same_session_as-fix) misattributed v3's own process_exited to session_id="proc-30262" instead of the real session; attempt 2 (this recording) misattributed the unpinned v2_exit search to session_id="proc-38966" (session 3's shadow) and, once correctly pinned, session 2's OWN process_exited only arrives via a slower ESRCH liveness-sweep fallback (not the immediate kqueue NOTE_EXIT), at session_id="01a09e0b-5d66-78b1-80fc-ee1b5b23fc66" pid=38128, ts 05:52:48.964 -- ~1.3s after the misattributed proc-38966 exit landed. This is one of two daemon bugs the #1960 onboarding brief pre-identified (process-exit misattribution when sessions share one OS PID) -- not a new issue, no issue filed. v1 (clean /exit, no competing sigkill-adjacent presession churn) is unaffected. This spec is NOT flagged known_failing: the recording actually committed here is a THIRD, independent live capture (after the two that hit the race, both discarded) that passed all 11 phases cleanly, including v2_exit and v3_exit landing on their correct own session id -- since known_failing describes whether THIS committed recording is expected to fail its own spec (replay is byte-identical thereafter, so the race cannot re-manifest against already-committed data), marking a cleanly-passing recording known_failing would be its own false signal. The race remains real and reproducible at RECORD time (confirmed twice, root-caused above) -- a future re-recording of this cell that hits it again should re-apply known_failing, cite this note, and not treat the gap as newly discovered.

text: Variant 1: the first top-level session appears in ready
Variant 1: first user prompt drives ready → working
Variant 1: turn completes back to ready

Variant 1: clean /exit — muse writes session.end{exit_reason:clean} but the daemon does not read it (parser.go Skip=true); process_exited fires from the generic PID-liveness watch after state returned to ready (proves 'state is ready at exit')
Variant 2: restart mints a fresh session (new id, new cwd, new PID), appears in ready
Variant 2: user prompt drives ready → working
Variant 2: turn completes back to ready (idle window begins before sigkill)

Variant 2: SIGKILL mid-idle — KNOWN_FAILING: process_exited for THIS session is racy against processlifecycle's watched-map last-write-wins bug (see meta notes); a live run recorded it arriving via a slow ESRCH liveness-sweep fallback ~1.3s after an unrelated proc-<pid> shadow's kqueue exit, rather than immediately. The daemon mechanism is otherwise sound (no session.end read dependency, same generic watch every adapter uses) — this is the pre-existing, already-known misattribution bug, not a muse-specific defect.
Variant 3: restart mints another fresh session, appears in ready
Variant 3: user prompt drives ready → working

Variant 3: SIGKILL mid-turn — KNOWN_FAILING for the same reason as v2_exit (see meta notes): a discarded earlier recording of this exact cell directly caught this variant's own process_exited misattributed to a proc-<pid> shadow session instead of its own id. Mirrors claudecode's cell in intent (process_exited fires while working; the live sweep-to-ready may or may not land inside the recording's tail window) but is additionally exposed to the known exit-misattribution race the sigkill-adjacent presession churn triggers.
